title: Load, stress, spike, soak and scalability: the difference

videos.script: Two teams both say they ran a load test. One held fifty requests a second for ten minutes. The other kept adding users until the server fell over. {{two}} Same tool. Same script. Different questions, and different meanings for a red result. {{same}} This lesson names five tests by the question each one asks. {{five}} Each has a shape, drawn as load against time. A steady line. A staircase that keeps climbing. A sudden spike and back. A flat line that lasts all night. And a staircase run twice, on a small machine and a bigger one. {{shapes}} Then you write a load generator small enough to read in a minute. {{code}} And you point it at the box office. Ten requests a second, and every page comes back in twenty milliseconds. Two hundred a second, and the same page takes seconds. {{spike}} Watch the seconds after the spike, too. The load is normal again, and the times are not. {{after}} Last, you give the box office one processor, then two, and see whether its capacity follows. {{scale}}
